tasks.short: Plan safety training and invite staff, run training sessions, demonstrate safety equipment, and record attendance.

steps.what: Safety specialist plans training sessions and invites staff by e-mail
Safety specialist conducts safety training programs in groups
Safety specialist demonstrates the use of safety equipment such as harnesses and respirators
Safety specialist types attendance from paper lists and files them

tasks.design: Sessions are planned in the learning system ({LMS}), which invites staff whose certificates are due and records attendance when staff sign in on a tablet at the session. Training and demonstrating equipment stay with the specialist; records are used for certificate expiry, not to rate staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Invitations went by e-mail and attendance was kept on paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems plan sessions, track expiry and record attendance.
tasks.still_hard: Shift workers are hard to get into one session.
tasks.human_edge: Showing on a real harness how a wrong buckle fails.

reach.learn: Whether expiry lists cut overdue certificates.

evidence.claim: Learning systems plan sessions, track certificate expiry and record attendance.
Arbo rules and systems that can monitor behaviour or performance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from training needs to attendance records; the training content is outside.
Input contract: training needs from the RI&E action plan kept by the specialist; staff lists from {HCM}; fallback is e-mail and paper.
Training and demonstrating do not change.
Staff sign-in time is about the same as a paper list.

incremental.description: Safety specialist corrects sign-in errors after sessions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is training in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather inspection notes, photos and incident records, compile figures, write the findings and causes, write recommendations, sign and send the report.

steps.what: Safety specialist gathers inspection notes, photos and incident records
Safety specialist compiles figures and tables for reports in a spreadsheet
Safety specialist writes the findings and causes

loop.input: Inspection notes, photos and the incident records for the case; no medical details.
loop.output: A draft narrative of what happened and what was found, each fact linked to a record.
loop.check: Code rejects facts without a record link; the specialist edits the draft and signs the report.
loop.stop: Signed by the specialist, or after two redrafts the specialist writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes and photos need turning into readable prose; a template cannot do that.

steps.what: Safety specialist writes recommendations and actions for the action plan
Safety specialist checks and signs the report
Safety specialist e-mails the report to management

tasks.design: Inspection notes and photos are taken on a tablet into the safety records app ({OTHER}) next to the incident records, and figures and tables come from the records by template. A bounded step drafts the narrative with each fact linked to a record; the specialist edits it, writes the recommendations and signs, and the signed report goes to management. Medical details stay out of the records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes, photos and spreadsheets were combined by hand into each report.
tasks.enabler_now: Safety records apps hold inspections and incidents, and language models draft from linked notes.
tasks.still_hard: Causes behind an incident often need interviews, not records.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that the real cause is a production target, not the worker.
tasks.altitude: The specialist edits a drafted narrative instead of writing it.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive sooner after an incident.

evidence.claim: Quentic's Reporting Assistant turns notes, photos and voice recordings into draft reports.
In LabSafety Bench no model passed 70% accuracy at hazard identification, so drafted safety text needs expert review.
The Dutch DPA fined a maintenance firm EUR 15,000 for recording the cause of employees' sickness.

assumptions: Boundary: from records to the report sent; carrying out actions is outside.
Input contract: incident records entered by line managers in the records app; inspection notes by the specialist; fallback is spreadsheets.
Recommendations and signing do not change.
Reports to the Labour Inspectorate are made at once and never wait on a draft.
research_questions: How much of the draft is kept?

already_counted.description: Safety specialist edits and checks the drafted narrative.

incremental.description: Safety specialist keeps report templates and record fields current.

approvals.approved_version: The report as signed by the specialist in s5; changes need a new signature before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Investigations with many interviews keep most of the writing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop orientation materials and a quiz from the RI&E and house rules, update them when rules change, give orientations to new employees, check understanding and record completion.

steps.what: Safety specialist develops materials for orientation presentations from the RI&E and house rules

loop.input: The current RI&E, house rules and emergency plan for the site.
loop.output: Slides, a one-page summary and a quiz, each point citing the section it rests on.
loop.check: Code rejects points without a cited section; the specialist edits and approves before use.
loop.stop: Approved by the specialist, or after two redrafts the specialist writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning risk assessments into plain teaching text needs rewording.

steps.what: Safety specialist updates materials when the RI&E or house rules change
Safety specialist provides new-employee health and safety orientations on site
Safety specialist checks understanding with a paper quiz and marks it
Safety specialist records completed orientations in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts slides, a summary and a quiz from the current RI&E and house rules, citing sections, and the specialist edits and approves them in the document space ({DOCS}), which flags materials when a source document changes. New employees take the quiz in the learning system ({LMS}), which scores it and records completion. Giving the orientation on site stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were built by hand and went out of date when rules changed.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft teaching text with section references.
tasks.still_hard: A model can miss or misstate hazards, so every draft needs expert review.
tasks.human_edge: Telling new staff the near-miss story that makes a rule stick.
tasks.altitude: The specialist edits drafted materials instead of building them.

reach.learn: Whether orientation completion shows in onboarding records.

evidence.claim: Mitti converts documents to inspection templates and translates training courses.
In LabSafety Bench no model passed 70% accuracy at hazard identification.
Employers must keep a written RI&E with an action plan.

assumptions: Boundary: from the RI&E to orientation records; job-specific training is outside.
Input contract: RI&E and house rules kept by the specialist; new starters from {HCM}; fallback is hand-built slides and paper quizzes.
Giving the orientation does not change.
New employees' quiz time is about the same on a tablet as on paper.

already_counted.description: Safety specialist edits and approves drafted materials.

incremental.description: Safety specialist reviews quiz results for common mistakes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The orientation itself stays in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get incident forms from line managers, enter them in the accident list, code cause, body part and location, build trend tables, analyze trends and discuss them with the safety committee.

steps.what: Line manager fills in the incident form and e-mails it
Safety specialist copies incident forms from e-mail into the accident list
Safety specialist codes cause, body part, location and days lost from each narrative

loop.input: The free-text incident narrative, without medical details.
loop.output: Codes for cause, body part and location with a confidence score.
loop.check: Codes below the confidence threshold go to the specialist; a monthly sample of auto-coded cases is checked.
loop.stop: One coding pass per incident; low-confidence cases are coded by the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narratives are written in many ways; keyword rules miscode them.

steps.what: Safety specialist builds trend tables and charts in a spreadsheet
Safety specialist analyzes incident data to identify trends in injuries, illnesses and hazards
Safety specialist discusses findings with the safety committee

tasks.design: Line managers enter incidents in a records app ({OTHER}) with fixed fields for location, days lost and severity, so nothing is copied from e-mail. A bounded step codes cause, body part and location from the narrative; below a confidence threshold the specialist codes it, as at the US labour statistics office. A dashboard ({BI}) shows trends by site, cause and period. Judging trends and discussing them with the committee stay with the specialist; medical details stay with the company doctor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms came by e-mail and were coded and counted by hand in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Models code injury narratives above a confidence threshold, and records apps feed dashboards.
tasks.still_hard: Small sites have too few incidents for clear trends.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that three minor cuts point to one badly placed machine.

ambition.what: Review trends monthly instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The specialist codes only unclear cases and spends time on trends.

reach.learn: Whether fixed fields cut incomplete reports.

evidence.claim: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics went from machine-coding 26% of occupation codes (2014) to about 92% of all codes (2021-22), assigning codes only above a confidence threshold.
Quentic Pattern Analysis flags recurring issues and hotspots in incident data.
The Dutch DPA fined a maintenance firm EUR 15,000 for recording the cause of employees' sickness, so medical details stay out of trend data.

assumptions: Boundary: from incident forms to committee actions; investigations are outside.
Input contract: incident forms entered by line managers with fixed fields; code list kept by the specialist; fallback is e-mailed forms.
Line managers already fill in a form; the app form takes about the same time, shown as other-role time.
research_questions: How often is the auto-code wrong in the monthly sample?

already_counted.description: Safety specialist codes low-confidence cases and checks the monthly sample.

incremental.description: Safety specialist keeps the code list and threshold current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Small sites gain little from coding.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The safety specialist keeps training, orientations, recommendations and judging trends; copying forms, coding, tables and hand-built materials shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A specialist who discusses trends each month instead of compiling them each year.
